language.script_notes: The coastal cities are the most linguistically homogeneous part of Peru, with less day-to-day Quechua than the highlands.
false_friends: Northern Chile (same coastal desert continuing south)

road_furniture.curb_style: Lima specifically features long, straight boulevard-style streets divided by a concrete or grassy median — unusual within Peru and a useful Lima-specific tell.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: The Pan-American Highway runs the length of the coastal strip.

architecture.roof_style: Flat roofs dominate given the near-total absence of rain; unfinished concrete/exposed rebar construction extremely common.
architecture.wall_construction: Dense informal multi-story concrete/brick construction in Lima's sprawling outer districts; more formal colonial-era architecture in Lima's historic center; desert oasis towns (Ica/Huacachina) further south.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Unpainted grey concrete/brick widely visible in newer districts; colonial pastel facades in central Lima.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Lima's colonial historic center (Plaza de Armas, balconied colonial buildings); dense unfinished concrete housing climbing the desert hillsides around Lima; desert oasis towns further south (Huacachina's sand dunes).

nature.vegetation: A narrow, mostly barren desert strip runs the length of the coast, green only in irrigated river valleys; almost no natural vegetation elsewhere.
nature.terrain: A flat-to-hilly coastal desert squeezed between the Pacific Ocean and the rising Andes foothills; Lima itself sits in a river valley oasis within this desert.
nature.climate_signature: Arid desert climate with a distinctive persistent grey coastal fog/overcast ('garúa') in Lima for much of the year despite almost no rainfall — a recognizable Lima-specific atmospheric signature.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Heaviest overall traffic density given Lima's population.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Best and most current coverage in the country, concentrated in and around Lima.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Very dense in Lima; good coverage along the Pan-American Highway corridor.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shares the same coastal desert stretching continuously across the border, similarly barren terrain
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Peru's striped sign poles and cigarette-shaped bollards differ from Chile's yellow-reflector road furniture; Peru's plates and tuktuks are absent in Chile.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The coast is flat, barren desert with Lima's persistent grey overcast; the highlands are cold and mountainous with visible Andean/Quechua culture, and the Amazon is dense green rainforest — all visually distinct.
